grammar_requirements.rule: Absence semantics for `git grep -c`/`git grep -l`: exit 1 with empty stdout means ZERO matches and yields the observed token "0". Every other empty-stdout-plus-nonzero-exit stays unobservable (a broken observation, not a red one). Scope the rule to argv whose argv[0:2] are git/grep and which carry -c or -l.
grammar_requirements.why: Three pairs here observe an absence (LC-04/05/13/14). The round-73 counter treated that as unobservable, so the BASEMISMATCH leg would fail on the honest observation. Freeze this before data; add a selftest with one present pattern (count printed) and one absent pattern (token 0, not unobservable).

grammar_requirements.rule: Observe allowlist = {git, grep, wc, sha256sum}. Drop python3: the round-73 survivor was a `python3 -c` constant printer, and no pair here needs an interpreter. Counting is done with `git diff --shortstat <empty-tree> <rev> -- '<glob>'` (prints 'N files changed') or `git grep -c`.
grammar_requirements.why: Round-73 routed defect 4 (ledger constant-printers). Also keeps every count re-derivable by hand.

grammar_requirements.rule: Revision discipline: an argv that must CHANGE between base and lands reads the graded tree (`HEAD`, or a repo-relative path); an argv that must NOT move pins the base revision by full 40-hex. The counter must reject a mutable ref (branch name) in place of the base hash.
grammar_requirements.why: Otherwise claim C's landing can move a Ca observation (the round-73 SEPARABLE hazard) or, conversely, an after-state can never turn green.

grammar_requirements.rule: statement re-reads (statement_after, and any 'latest value' read) take the LAST occurrence in the file, via the DOTALL `(?s).*PATTERN` idiom. Fixture: a file with two 'Total knowledge entries:' lines, the first stale — the read must return the second.
grammar_requirements.why: corpus/README.md carries two footers (`:732` 243, `:775` 247) and two counts-checked blocks; `reports/round-28/readme/sweep.py` exits 1 on the base tree for reading the first.

grammar_requirements.rule: Fleet stated side: a pair may carry `stated_fleet` {path, line, pin, sha256} and a stated_at of the form `fleet:<path>:<line>`. The counter must branch BEFORE the lane path:line check (otherwise the `fleet:` prefix is read as a lane path and the LEDGER leg fails), resolve with `git -C <fleet_root> show <pin>:<path>`, validate stated_text on that line, and also assert the report bytes at fleet HEAD equal the pinned sha256 with zero removed lines.
grammar_requirements.why: LC-03 states its claim in the fleet report, which the lane cannot edit; the round-73 counter could only read lane files, so this class had no home. Pin must contain the file (see fleet_pin_note).

grammar_requirements.rule: CONTENTPIN leg: each content_pins entry must (a) at <lands> observe exactly expected_after, and (b) at base observe something DIFFERENT. For a sha256 pin the base token is the base content hash; for the presence pin (argv git ls-tree over one path) empty stdout means absence and is recorded as the sentinel "absent", which counts as different. A pin that is already green at base is dropped, never kept. The pin is also recorded as blob ids so the TRACKED leg can check the same content without relying on checkout filters.
grammar_requirements.why: The six round-73 wave-2 seat files are a content defect, not a prose defect: there is no document statement whose token could be compared, so they cannot ride the BASEMISMATCH leg honestly (a hash-versus-word 'mismatch' would be trivially red and worthless).

grammar_requirements.rule: Make the drop rule a leg: the counter FAILS if any pair (or content pin) is green at base. Round 73 only required `mismatched >= min_pairs`, so green pairs could ride along.
grammar_requirements.why: The claim's stated before-state is 'EVERY listed pair red'. A pair that is green at base is a false claim of redness.

grammar_requirements.rule: SEPARABLE operand: keep the round-73 whole-ledger scan for claim-C paths and for S-ids >= the frozen separator, and freeze that separator explicitly for round 74: read the lowest row id the coverage claim appends this round from the frozen claims file and use that (do not copy round 73's 876, which would let this round's own appended rows be cited). This draft cites no id above S880, so a separator of 881 keeps it clean. State in the counter whether a base-pinned read of a C artefact is still a C path; this draft assumes YES and avoids the registry file entirely.
grammar_requirements.why: The scan is a string scan, so `stated_at` alone can trip it: the honest pair for the registry row S879 had to be anchored on the lesson instead (LC-11). If the L1 freezes a different separator the pair set still holds.

grammar_requirements.rule: Read the counter's own constants from the frozen commit, not from the graded tree (round-73 routed defect 4, survivor 1): CLAIM/SEPARABLE/MIN_PAIRS/paths must come from the ledger + frozen assets, and the counter must refuse a ledger that names a different claim or round.
grammar_requirements.why: A graded-tree config lets a landing edit the predicate it is graded by.
